claim: IoPC is a small MQTT-only PC-integration service (Kotlin/Gradle with a native component, GPL-3.0, 40 stars, 16 commits) that HASS.Agent's own README recommends as its Linux alternative
stance_target: the Linux HA-agent ecosystem's second reference point is a minimal MQTT service bus, validating MQTT-first design as the viable Linux-native pattern (versus go-hass-agent's dual transport)
scope_conditions: IoPC master branch; recommended but explicitly untested by the HASS.Agent team
quoted_support: Now it supports MQTT protocol, so you can integrate IoPC with HomeAssistant. ... You can try the official companion app for macOS, or IoPC which runs on Linux.

claim: IoPC's MQTT design is a two-prefix service bus: inbound commands on {PREFIX}/{CLIENT_ID}/command/# with JSON {service, payload} envelopes, outbound sensor values on {PREFIX}/{CLIENT_ID}/#, configured via web UI (127.0.0.1:60555) or IOPC_MQTT_* env vars
stance_target: a clean minimal topic grammar + JSON service envelope is a legitimate alternative to HA MQTT-discovery semantics; ha-linux-agent should compare its topic layout against both this and HA discovery
scope_conditions: IoPC defaults: PREFIX=iopc, CLIENT_ID per host
quoted_support: By default, inbound MQTT prefix for IoPC instance is {MQTT_PREFIX}/{MQTT_CLIENT_ID}/command/#. ... For example, we want to set PC volume from HomeAssistant. We should send following message to topic iopc/myComputer/command/homeassistant {"service": "volume.set", "payload": {"volume": 54}}

claim: IoPC sensors are NOT updated automatically — a service call (e.g. volume.get) must be invoked to refresh sensor values; the sensor set is availability state, volume, RAM free/total, CPU usage %, per-drive info, lastUserInput, and an activity state machine (active/idle at 30s/away at 5min)
stance_target: poll-on-demand-only sensor publishing is inadequate for a fleet agent; ha-linux-agent must have scheduled/event-driven publishing (the user's 'never reliable' complaint would be worsened by this design)
quoted_support: For now, sensors are not updated automatically, so you should run a special service to update sensor value. ... activity/state: User state. Can be active, idle (if not active for 30sec), away (if not active for 5min), unknown
